page: Amazon Web Services x2iedn.16xlarge is a memory-optimized server powered by an Intel Xeon 8375C processor with 64 vCPUs and 32 physical cores built on the x86_64 architecture. Running on the Nitro hypervisor, the instance features 2048 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, translating to 32 GB of RAM per physical core. Local storage is provided via a 1900 GB NVMe SSD, and network connectivity delivers a baseline bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and database performance. The server achieves a top-tier PassMark CPU score of 56,826.42 and a PassMark database operations score of 26,144.88. Multi-threaded decompression and software compilation benchmarks also rank in the top 25%. Conversely, single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the average category. Memory bandwidth tests, such as large-block uncached reads at 153.34 GB/sec, also align with average tier performance.

The high memory-to-vCPU ratio offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads by reducing the need to scale up vCPU counts solely to acquire more RAM. This resource density makes the instance suitable for large in-memory databases, enterprise-grade relational databases, big data analytics, and memory-bound electronic design automation applications. However, for workloads primarily constrained by single-thread CPU speed rather than memory capacity, the average single-core performance represents a potential efficiency tradeoff.
